gaps.sentence: There were ___ than twenty people at the meeting.
The night bus runs ___ twenty minutes.
gaps.explanation: 'Every twenty minutes' expresses regular intervals; 'each twenty minutes' is not used.

gaps.sentence: We need to find ___ who can fix the boiler.
gaps.hint: affirmative statement: an unknown but existing person
gaps.explanation: 'Someone' is used in affirmative sentences; 'anyone' belongs to questions and negatives.

gaps.sentence: He had ___ money, so he couldn't even buy a bus ticket.
gaps.explanation: 'Had no money' states zero and explains the result; 'none' cannot stand directly before a noun.

gaps.sentence: ___ candidate was given five minutes to speak.
gaps.hint: one at a time, singular verb
gaps.explanation: 'Each candidate was given' — singular agreement; 'all candidate' is wrong.

gaps.sentence: Very ___ applicants had the required experience.
gaps.hint: 'very' + negative quantifier with a countable plural
gaps.explanation: 'Very few' means almost none and is used with countables; 'very a few' is impossible.
'Some' is used in offers and requests where we expect agreement; 'any' is for neutral questions.

gaps.sentence: ___ of my friends knew about the concert, so I went on my own.
gaps.explanation: 'None of my friends' means zero friends; 'no' cannot stand before 'of' and 'nothing' is not a quantifier here.
